newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-ENGLAND CAN REGROUP, SAYS ATHERTON.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ENGLAND CAN REGROUP, SAYS ATHERTON.

text.p: England captain Mike Atherton was confident on Wednesday his team could regroup for the second test against New Zealand after Sunday's embarrassing loss to the nation's second-string side.

Following their disastrous display in Zimbabwe, where they were trounced in the one-day series and managed only draws in the two tests, England's tour had looked to be back on the rails with two early wins in New Zealand.

But it slipped off again in the first test when England allowed New Zealand a miraculous escape with a draw thanks to a record 10th wicket stand of 106 by Nathan Astle and the world record holder for ducks, Danny Morrison.

England were then emphatically beaten by New Zealand A by 90 runs in Wanganui last weekend, but Atherton said that would have no bearing on their prospects in the second test, starting at the Basin Reserve in Wellington on Thursday.
"Games in between tests are hard games, particularly when you're playing a side like New Zealand A," Atherton said.
"They had 11 cricketers busting their guts to get in a test match and there were five or six of our side who played in the first test at Auckland who were pretty jaded.
Atherton said it was too much to expect players to give their absolute best for 15 days on the trot.
"It's hard to ask players to do that. You've always got to keep something in reserve," he said.
But Atherton said he was confident his players would respond to the challenge.
"Our test match form is pretty good. If we perform over a period of time, then little slices of fortune will turn our way and the results will follow," he said.
England had a setback when fast-medium bowler Chris Silverwood, one of the few England players to perform well at Wanganui, was ruled out by a hand injury.
Silverwood looked in line to take over from either Alan Mullally or Craig White who both bowled erratically in the Auckland test. New Zealand-born Andrew Caddick may now come into the reckoning.
New Zealand's preparations were also disrupted by an ankle injury to all-rounder Chris Cairns. A decision on whether he can play will be made later on Wednesday.
If he fails a fitness test, part-time leg-spinner Chris Harris may be thrust into the all-rounder role and most interest will centre on whether teenage spinner Daniel Vettori is included.
Just past his 18th birthday, and with only two first class games to his credit, the bespectacled left-armer is expected to play and become New Zealand's youngest test player.

In one other change, left-arm seamer Geoff Allott, main wicket taker in the destruction of England in Wanganui, replaces Morrison, whose batting heroics in the first test failed to mask his poor bowling form.
